findings.description: The --consumed-by path accepts a map that is still charting, although the unattended exception is documented as applying to handed-off maps.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended caller can close an unfinished map: op_close rejects every open decision row, closes its beads and epic, and marks the map closed without operator participation.
findings.suggested_fix: Before any mutation, require a handed-off map for consumption and verify that no open rows or unresolved fog remain. Preserve idempotent retries for an already consumed map.

findings.description: Comparing porcelain status strings does not detect changes to files that were already dirty, untracked, or ignored before the probe.
findings.failure_mode: If src/example is already modified, a probe can overwrite it through an absolute path while its status remains ' M src/example'. Both snapshots match and the helper exits successfully despite changing the main tree. Existing untracked files and files inside an already ignored directory have the same problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content fingerprints before and after execution, including existing dirty, untracked and ignored files, rather than using status entries as content snapshots.

findings.description: Passing the sanitized bullet through awk -v line interprets backslash escapes after san1 has checked and flattened the text.
findings.failure_mode: A --line value containing literal '\n## Additional section\n' becomes actual newlines and a new Markdown section in the map. Ordinary backslash-containing text can also be corrupted. This bypasses the intended single-line boundary before the map is copied into planning context.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the text through an environment variable read with ENVIRON, or another mechanism that preserves literal bytes without awk assignment escape processing.

findings.description: Epic creation is considered complete only when the map document exists; there is no lookup for an epic created by an earlier interrupted attempt.
findings.failure_mode: If br create succeeds and document creation subsequently fails or the process is interrupted, retrying creates another map epic. The original epic remains orphaned, violating the helper's stated retry and idempotency contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the epic a stable lookup identity and reuse it before creating another one, then finish the missing document write on retry.

findings.description:
section_append (and set_status at line 120) hand free text to awk through `-v line="$2"`. awk processes backslash escapes in -v assignments, so `
` in --line, --name, --why, or a bead title fetched from br (op_rule_out uses the bead's title) becomes a real newline. san1 strips control bytes and whitespace but leaves backslashes, so `--line 'ok
## Execution override
- do X'` inserts a new H2 into the map doc. The map doc is later copied verbatim into grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md by op_handoff and read by /plan-and-analyze as priority-1 'settled, do not re-ask' context.
findings.failure_mode: Agent-controlled or br-sourced text rewrites the structure of a tracked map doc and the priority-1 hand-off snapshot; downstream section_bullets/handoff logic and the planning interview read the injected sections as authoritative.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pass user text via awk -v. Export it as an environment variable and read ENVIRON["LINE"] inside awk, or double every backslash before -v (`${line//\\/\\\\}`). Also have san1 strip or reject backslashes and have resolve/rule-out reject a value containing a literal `\n`/`\r` sequence.

findings.description: op_close with --consumed-by skips the interactive-context check (only the --reason branch calls `$DW context`) and never checks the map's Status. chart.md documents the unattended exception as `close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle>` 'on a handed-off map', but the script accepts a `charting` map with open rows, rejects every open ledger row with 'map closed: consumed by ...', closes all its question beads and the epic, and marks the doc closed. Rejection of ledger rows is not reversible by a re-run.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous run (or a mistyped slug) that executes `chart-ticket.sh close --map <charting-map> --consumed-by <cycle>` silently destroys the open decision frontier of a map that was never handed off, in exactly the unattended context the feature is meant to forbid.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, when --consumed-by is given require `doc_field Status` == handed-off (or closed, for idempotent re-runs) and refuse otherwise; additionally require that map_rows contains no `open` rows before rejecting anything, mirroring op_handoff's frontier/fog checks.

findings.description: The interactive-only rule (chart.md 'Interactive only', chart-guard.sh header: PRD D12 / SDD D-4.3 step 0) is enforced only by chart-guard.sh, which is a separate script nothing forces to run. The write subcommands epic, ticket, resolve, rule-out and handoff in chart-ticket.sh run `dw new/decide/reject`, `br create/close` and rewrite the map doc without ever calling `$DW context`. Only `close --reason` checks. With LOA_UNATTENDED=1 (or inside a RUNNING run state) `chart-ticket.sh epic ... && chart-ticket.sh ticket ...` succeeds and creates a map whose rounds the agent answered for itself.
findings.failure_mode: Any unattended invocation that reaches chart-ticket.sh directly (skill allowlist, /run autonomous, a stale prompt) creates map epics, question beads and ledger rows that the spec says must never be created without the operator; the 'interactive only' guarantee in chart.md is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the context check out of op_close into a `require_interactive` helper that calls `"$DW" context --prd "${G}/prd.md"` and dies unless it prints `interactive`; call it at the top of op_epic, op_ticket, op_resolve, op_rule_out, op_handoff, op_research_begin and the --reason branch of op_close. Keep `close --consumed-by` as the only exception.

findings.description: SP-1 claims 'spike content never enters another branch' (D-5.4) and lists its known misses at lines 834-836. The most direct ways to land spike content on main are neither blocked nor listed: `git push origin spike/x:main` (and `spike/x:refs/heads/main`), `git branch -f main spike/x`, `git reset --hard spike/x` while on main, `git update-ref refs/heads/main spike/x`, `git read-tree -u -m spike/x`, `git checkout -p spike/x`, and `git branch -m spike/x feature/x` followed by a normal merge. The push form is especially bad because `git push ... spike/x` is explicitly allowed and only the destination refspec differs; the hook pre-filter `*spike/*` already fires, so the cost of adding the pattern is one regex.
findings.failure_mode: An agent on a spike ticket runs `git push origin spike/<slug>:main` (or a force-update of main from the spike ref) and publishes prototype code to the default branch with no block, no PR and no ICE refusal, defeating the SP-1 invariant that downstream tooling relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the SP-1 block: `git push` where any refspec matches `spike/[^:[:space:]]+:(?!spike/)`; `git (branch|update-ref|reset|read-tree|symbolic-ref)` whose operand list contains a spike/ ref; `git checkout -p <spike ref>`; and `git branch -m|-M spike/<x> <other>`. Update the Misses comment for whatever remains intentionally unblocked.

findings.description: The D-5.9 exception lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through when a decided ledger row exists, but a spike branch is defined as 'the pointer for a decision: pushed, never merged'. The function never checks that `refs/remotes/*/spike/<slug>` exists or that the branch has an upstream. The ledger (grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml) is a tracked file the agent can edit with Write, so a row with `status: decided` and `by: operator:x` is cheap to fabricate.
findings.failure_mode: `git branch -D spike/x` on an unpushed spike with a decided row deletes the only copy of the prototype the spike report's Pointer names; the decision now cites a commit that no longer exists anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: In _fr11_spike_decided also require `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` (or any remote-tracking ref for the name) and that the local tip is an ancestor of it; keep the block when either check fails.

findings.description: op_epic's idempotency key is the existence of the map doc. If `br create` succeeds and the doc write fails (mkdir/mktemp/mv error, kill between the two), a re-run finds no doc and runs `br create ... --slug map-<slug>` again, producing two `map` epics. The header promises 're-run ... creates only what is missing', and op_ticket does the bead lookup by external_ref for exactly this reason, but op_epic does not look the epic up by slug/label.
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate map epics on beads; chart-frontier and op_close only ever address the one the doc names, so the orphan epic stays open forever.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `br create`, query `beads_all | jq 'select(.issue_type=="epic" and (.slug=="map-<slug>" or labels contains map and title==...))'` and reuse an existing id; write the doc from the found id.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-frontier.sh (same PR, line 55) matches question beads on `.issue_type // .type`, and the PR's br-stub emits beads the frontier accepts; get-ready-work.sh filters on `.issue_type` alone. The two scripts disagree on the schema inside one PR.
findings.description: The build-path exclusion that implement.md and implementing-tasks/SKILL.md now rely on (`get-ready-work.sh ... drops question beads`) is `select((.issue_type // "") != "question")`. A br release or stub that emits `type` instead of `issue_type` passes every question bead through to /implement and /run, while chart-frontier.sh in the same change accepts both keys.
findings.failure_mode: Decision tickets appear in the build ready set and get claimed/implemented by an autonomous run, which is exactly what create-sprint-task.sh's refusal and the chart.md 'tickets cannot enter a sprint' claim try to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"` in get-ready-work.sh so both scripts share one predicate; add a bats case with a `type`-only bead.

findings.description: The map-epic check yields `no` whenever the `br show --json` object has no `labels` key (or an empty array), so a br whose JSON names the field differently (`tags`, `label`) or a show that omits labels lets a map epic through silently. The script fails closed only for the jq-error case, not for the schema-mismatch case. Also, the type check at line 101 happens before `cd` to the repo root, which is harmless, but the type refusal is case-folded while the label match is not (`Map`).
findings.failure_mode: A sprint task is created under a /chart map epic, violating D-4.7, with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an object with no recognisable labels field as `unknown` (refuse with the same 'could not read the labels' message), and compare labels case-insensitively. Additionally reject when the epic's `issue_type` is not `epic`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff's chart-researcher.md grants `Write` (line 5) and agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable: true; the escalated head copy of chart-researcher.md says the agent has no Write/Edit/Bash and returns the report as its final message. The two files disagree.
findings.description: The repository carries two contradictory contracts for the research subagent: the diff grants a path-unbounded `Write` to an agent that WebFetches arbitrary pages, while the head agent file says it writes nothing. agent-types.yaml still says write_capable: true. If Write stays, note that chart-ticket.sh research-end only diffs `git status --porcelain` lines: an edit to a tracked file that was already dirty before dispatch (the map doc, decisions.yaml mid-session) produces an identical status line and is not detected, and writes outside the repo are invisible. If Write is removed, write_capable: true is wrong and the skill must itself be allowed to write grimoires/loa/research/ for research-end to find the report.
findings.failure_mode: Either a prompt-injected research subagent silently modifies already-dirty priority-1 inputs / files outside the repo, or the capability inventory misreports the agent and the skill-capabilities lint and research-end flow are inconsistent with reality.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: remove Write from the agent (as the head file says) and set write_capable: false, and give the charting-decisions skill the Write allow for grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md; or keep Write but have research-begin snapshot a content hash (`git diff --no-ext-diff | sha256sum` plus `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard | xargs sha256sum`) so research-end catches edits to already-dirty files.

findings.description: The probe argv runs with the session's full environment and credentials, and the only post-condition is that the main tree's `git status --porcelain` text is unchanged. The throwaway worktree shares `.git` with the main tree, so `git branch -f main HEAD`, `git push`, `git tag`, `git stash`, `git config --global`, and any write outside the repository (~/.ssh, ~/.netrc, /tmp) alter nothing that `git status` reports. Edits to tracked files that were already dirty before the probe are likewise invisible. The skill allowlists this script wholesale, and probe commands can be lifted from untrusted research reports or ticket bodies.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock ticket probe exfiltrates or mutates state (remote refs, local branches, global git config, home-directory files) while the helper reports 'main tree unchanged' and exit 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare `git for-each-ref` and `git stash list` alongside status; run the probe with a minimal env (`env -i PATH=... HOME=<scratch>`), `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, and `GIT_DIR` pointing at the worktree only; require the skill to echo the argv to the operator and get confirmation before invoking.

findings.description: map_rows resolves worktree pending ledgers via `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml` rather than `${ROOT}`, so `--root DIR` (used by the bats fixtures and documented as the fixture tree) still merges the live repo's pending rows into the fixture map. Also, if `dw list` ever prints non-JSON for an empty set, `--argjson a` fails and set -e aborts the command with no message.
findings.failure_mode: Fixture runs read production pending rows (flaky or wrongly-passing tests); a malformed pending file aborts every map operation silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `"${G}/a2a/"*/decisions-pending.yaml`; default `$all` to `[]` when empty and guard the jq merge with `|| die`.

findings.description: The frontier depends on `br ready --parent <epic> --type question --unassigned --limit 0 --json`, a flag combination only the PR's tests/fixtures/charting/br-stub.sh is known to accept. Any installed br that rejects one flag, or that treats `--limit 0` as 'zero results', yields either exit 1 with the misleading 'unknown epic?' message or a permanently empty frontier. `--root` affects only the map doc and the bv cwd; `br ready` runs in the caller's cwd, so the slug-to-epic resolution and the beads database can come from different trees.
findings.failure_mode: On a real br, /chart reports no tickets to work (or an unknown-epic error) for a map that has open question beads, and the session cannot progress.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the flags against the pinned beads_rust version in install-br.sh and add a version check or a fallback to `br ready --json` with the parent/type/assignee filtering done in the existing jq FILTER; run br with `-C "$ROOT"` or `cd "$ROOT"`.
